questions.text: Your mummy is forcing you to eat a huge bowl of Dal and Paneer because 'it makes you strong'. What is your reaction?

options.A: You eat it quickly and immediately drop to the floor to do 20 pushups to build muscle.
options.B: You mentally calculate the exact grams of protein in the paneer to see if it hits your daily required macros.
options.C: You eat it slowly without looking at your phone, focusing on chewing properly for good digestion and gut health.
options.D: You take an aesthetic top-angle photo of the 'Desi Diet', add a trending Punjabi song, and post it on your Instagram.

questions.text: You go to the local society park early in the morning. What are you most likely doing?

options.A: Hanging on the monkey bars doing pull-ups and challenging your friends to a 100-meter sprint.
options.B: Checking your smartwatch every 5 minutes to ensure your heart rate is in the fat-burning zone and tracking your steps.
options.C: Finding a quiet spot on the grass to do Anulom Vilom, deep stretching, and enjoying the fresh morning air.
options.D: Looking at the rusted open-air gym equipment and thinking about how much money a proper AC gym in this colony would make.

questions.text: Your friend wants to look good in a Sherwani/Lehenga for an upcoming cousin's wedding in 2 months. How do you help them?

options.A: You force them to wake up at 6 AM every day and drag them out of bed for a heavy jog.
options.B: You strictly ban them from eating roadside momos and create a daily chart of what they should eat for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
options.C: You teach them posture-correcting exercises so they stand taller, look more graceful, and don't slouch in the photos.
options.D: You hype them up, take their 'before' pictures, and promise them that everyone at the wedding will be shocked by their glow-up.

questions.text: When you are scrolling through fitness reels on Instagram or YouTube, what hooks your attention?

options.A: Intense desi akhara workouts, heavy deadlifts, and people pushing their physical limits to the max.
options.B: Videos debunking diet myths, explaining why sugar is bad, or reviewing which protein powder is actually genuine.
options.C: Aesthetic morning routine vlogs featuring Surya Namaskar, calming music, and natural remedies for glowing skin.
options.D: Fitness influencers who got sponsored by big brands, launched their own clothing lines, and bought luxury cars.

questions.text: Your school's PT (Physical Training) period gets cancelled because it's raining. What do you do?

options.A: Start an intense arm-wrestling or plank-holding competition at the back benches of the classroom.
options.B: Use the free time to secretly open your tiffin box and eat your boiled eggs or sprouts exactly on time.
options.C: Sit quietly, stretch your stiff neck and shoulders, and take a 5-minute mental break from studying.
options.D: Use the time to plan a weekend cricket tournament and start collecting the entry fees from your classmates.

questions.text: What is your take on the classic 'Desi Ghee vs. Olive Oil' debate at home?

options.A: It doesn't matter what you eat as long as you hit the gym hard and sweat it out completely!
options.B: You analyze the fat profiles, comparing the exact calorie count and nutritional benefits of both to see which is scientifically better.
options.C: You believe Desi Ghee is an ancient Ayurvedic practice that naturally lubricates the joints and heals the body from within.
options.D: You notice how fitness brands cleverly market olive oil as 'premium' just so they can charge double the price.

questions.text: You walk into a local neighborhood gym for the very first time. What catches your eye immediately?

options.A: The heavy dumbbells, the bench press area, and the trainers physically spotting guys lifting weights.
options.B: The diet charts pinned on the notice board and the rows of supplement boxes being sold at the reception.
options.C: The empty, mirrored studio room where people can stretch quietly away from all the loud music and clanking iron.
options.D: The monthly membership fees written on the whiteboard and calculating how many people are currently working out.

questions.text: You sprain your ankle while playing badminton. How do you deal with the recovery?

options.A: You get extremely restless, do upper-body workouts while sitting on a chair, and desperately wait to get back on the court.
options.B: You increase your Vitamin C and calcium intake so your ligaments and bones heal faster on a biological level.
options.C: You do gentle rehabilitation movements, use hot-water bags, and practice mindful breathing to manage the pain gracefully.
options.D: You vlog your recovery journey on Instagram, using trending audio to gain views and new followers.

questions.text: It's time for the annual school marathon (cross-country). What is your main focus?

options.A: Running extra laps during practice and physically pushing your friends to run faster so your house wins.
options.B: Planning exactly what to eat the night before (carb-loading) and mixing Electoral powder in your water bottle.
options.C: Teaching your friends how to stretch their hamstrings properly so they don't get cramps midway through the race.
options.D: Designing a cool, custom team jersey for your squad so you guys look like the most professional team out there.

questions.text: Honestly, what sounds like the coolest achievement when you grow up?

options.A: Having a highly muscular, athletic body that instantly commands respect when you walk into any room.
options.B: Being the genius who completely transforms sick people into healthy athletes just by changing what they eat.
options.C: Being extremely flexible, peaceful, and living a stress-free life where you can heal others holistically.
options.D: Owning the biggest, most premium gym in your city, having thousands of members, and becoming a famous fitness brand.

Personal_Trainer.title: The Iron Coach (Personal Trainer / CrossFit Coach)
Personal_Trainer.primary_match_text: You are pure energy! You love physical movement, lifting heavy, and pushing your body to its absolute limits. As a Personal Trainer or CrossFit Coach, you would be the motivator on the gym floor, demonstrating exercises, fixing forms, and physically helping people achieve their dream bodies.
Personal_Trainer.day_in_the_life: Your day starts at 5 AM. You are on the gym floor, wearing tracks, holding a stopwatch, and screaming 'One more rep!' to your clients. You spend your day working out, teaching proper lifting techniques, and seeing people grow stronger every single month.
Personal_Trainer.alternative_match_text: If not a Gym Trainer, you would make an amazing Sports Coach, Physical Education (PT) Teacher, or Stunt Coordinator.
Personal_Trainer.educational_roadmap: Take any stream in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.P.Ed (Bachelor of Physical Education) or any graduation degree. The most important step is clearing professional certifications from reputed bodies like K11 Academy, Gold's Gym Fitness Institute, or ACE (American Council on Exercise).

Sports_Nutritionist.title: The Macro Master (Sports Nutritionist / Dietician)
Sports_Nutritionist.primary_match_text: You are highly analytical and believe that bodies are made in the kitchen, not just the gym! You love the science behind food. As a Sports Nutritionist, you would calculate exact proteins, fats, and carbs to build customized diet charts that help athletes perform at their peak.
Sports_Nutritionist.day_in_the_life: You sit in a clinic or a high-end sports facility. A state-level cricketer comes to you wanting to increase stamina. You analyze their blood reports, calculate their caloric needs, and create a strict, scientific meal plan down to the last gram of paneer.
Sports_Nutritionist.alternative_match_text: If not a Sports Nutritionist, you would thrive as a Clinical Dietician, Food Scientist, or Health Researcher.
Sports_Nutritionist.educational_roadmap: Take Science (PCB - Physics, Chemistry, Biology) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc in Nutrition & Dietetics or Home Science. Follow it up with an M.Sc in Sports Nutrition or specialized diplomas from the Sports Authority of India (SAI).

Yoga_Instructor.title: The Holistic Healer (Yoga & Mobility Instructor)
Yoga_Instructor.primary_match_text: You are creative, calm, and value flexibility over raw strength. You believe fitness is about the mind just as much as the body. As a Yoga and Mobility Instructor, you would focus on breathwork, beautiful postures, and holistic healing to fix people's stress and body pains.
Yoga_Instructor.day_in_the_life: Your day involves peaceful, well-lit studio rooms with soft music. You guide a class of 30 people through complex Vinyasa flows, correcting their postures, teaching them how to breathe deeply, and helping them find mental peace after a stressful workday.
Yoga_Instructor.alternative_match_text: If not a Yoga Instructor, you would excel as a Physiotherapist, Wellness Coach, or Pilates Expert.
Yoga_Instructor.educational_roadmap: Take any stream in 11th/12th. Pursue a BA or B.Sc in Yoga and Naturopathy (available in many Indian universities). Get certified by the Ministry of AYUSH (Yoga Certification Board) or complete a 200-hour Teacher Training Course (TTC) from Yoga Alliance.

Gym_Owner.title: The Fitness Mogul (Gym Owner / Fitness Influencer)
Gym_Owner.primary_match_text: You are a born entrepreneur! You see fitness not just as a lifestyle, but as a massive booming business. As a Gym Owner or Fitness Influencer, you would focus on building a brand, selling premium memberships, marketing supplements, and leading a fitness empire.
Gym_Owner.day_in_the_life: You are not just lifting weights; you are lifting profits. You manage the gym staff, negotiate deals for importing new treadmills, collaborate with supplement brands for Instagram reels, and strategize how to get 500 new members before New Year's Eve.
Gym_Owner.alternative_match_text: If not in the Fitness industry, you would be a brilliant Startup Founder, Marketing Head, or Event Manager.
Gym_Owner.educational_roadmap: Take Commerce or any stream in 11th/12th. Pursue a BBA, B.Com, or a degree in Mass Communication. A Master's in Business Administration (MBA) in Marketing or Sports Management will give you the exact skills needed to build and scale a massive fitness franchise in India.
